verdict: Strong close-in demand and fuller ships (112% load factor) pushed revenue up 9% to $5.6B and profit to $1.73B, so the company raised its full-year earnings guidance.

kpis.label: Load factor
kpis.note: Ships sailed more than full on a double-occupancy basis; 2.7M guests, +9% YoY

segments.name: Passenger ticket revenues
segments.note: What guests pay for their cruise fares

segments.name: Onboard and other revenues
segments.note: What guests spend on board and before sailing — drinks, excursions, spa, specialty dining and more

opex.name: Marketing, selling and administrative
opex.note: Marketing, selling and head-office costs, including $9M of restructuring charges

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of ships and other assets over their lives

flow.otherDetail: Other income is interest expense, net of interest capitalized ($291M), partly offset by equity investment income ($176M, mainly its TUI Cruises joint venture), interest income ($5M) and $1M of other income. Equity is minus $7M of profit belonging to noncontrolling interests, so net income is the $1,728M attributable to Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. (total net income was $1,735M).

takeaways.title: Revenue grew with fuller, bigger capacity
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose to $5,591M from $5,139M a year ago, with capacity up 8% and 2.7 million guests carried, up 9%.

takeaways.title: Ships sailed over full
takeaways.text: Load factor was 112%, and onboard and other revenue grew 14% to $1,706M as guests spent more before and during their cruises.

takeaways.title: Profit rose and guidance went up
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to the company was $1,728M, or $6.45 per share, versus $1,575M a year ago, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $17.85–$17.95.

oneTimers: Loss on extinguishment of debt of $21M in the quarter, included in interest expense (excluded from adjusted results)
Restructuring charges and other initiative expenses of $9M, included in marketing, selling and administrative expenses
footerNote: Cost of revenue here is total cruise operating expenses (commissions and transportation, onboard costs, payroll, food, fuel and other operating costs), following Royal Caribbean's own gross-margin presentation, which also deducts depreciation before gross margin in its non-GAAP yield tables — depreciation is shown as an operating expense in this flow instead, so operating income matches the reported $1,871M.
follow100Note: Other income in this breakdown combines the other-income and equity lines from the flow, so the rows add to the net margin. Percentages are rounded to two decimals, so rows may differ from the kept-as-profit row by 0.01.
